instructions.text: In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, combine the melted palm shortening, maple syrup, and coconut sugar. Mix on medium speed until well combined and smooth.
Add the egg and vanilla extract to the mixture in the stand mixer bowl. Mix on medium speed until thoroughly incorporated.

Add almond flour, coconut flour, arrowroot, baking powder, baking soda, and a pinch of salt. Mix on high speed for 1 minute (no less!), stopping to scrape down the sides if necessary. Fold in chocolate chips using a spatula. Set the dough aside to rest and allow the coconut flour to absorb some of the moisture. Wipe down the bowl quickly to use for the brownie batter.
Preheat the oven to 325 degrees. Line a 9x9 inch baking dish with parchment paper or lightly grease it.
Start by melting the palm shortening on the stove. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in the chocolate pieces until smooth. Let the mixture cool.
In the stand mixer with a whisk attachment, beat the eggs for 5 minutes on high speed until they become fluffy and pale. DO NOT BEAT LESS THAN 5 MINUTES.
While the eggs are being beaten, measure the maple sugar and coconut sugar, then add to the beaten eggs. Continue beating until well combined, 30 seconds to a minute.
Gradually add the cooled chocolate and palm shortening mixture to the beaten eggs and sugar, mixing until thoroughly incorporated. Stir in the vanilla extract.

Add almond flour, arrowroot powder, coconut flour, Dutch process chocolate, salt, and baking powder to the mixture. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture with a rubber spatula until just combined. Be careful not to overmix.
If desired, fold in additional chocolate chips into the batter.
Spread the brownie batter evenly into the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Drop spoonfuls of the cookie dough all around the top of the brownie batter and push a few into the brownie batter, leaving some on top with ribbons of brownie batter undisturbed.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 50 minutes, covering with foil after 30 minutes if the cookie layer is beginning to brown too much.
Once baked, remove from the oven and let cool completely in the baking dish before slicing into squares and serving.

Brookies - Gluten and Dairy-Free

Cook time
50 mins
Total time
50 mins
 
Author: Amy Simonsen
Recipe type: Dessert
Serves: 14
Ingredients
  • Cookie Layer
  • ¼ cup (45g) palm shortening, melted
  • ¼ cup (77g) maple syrup
  • ¼ cup (41g) coconut sugar
  • 1 large egg, room temperature
  • 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
  • 1 cup (100g) blanched almond flour
  • 2½ teaspoons coconut flour
  • 1 tablespoon arrowroot powder
  • ½ teaspoon baking powder
  • ¼ teaspoon baking soda
  • Pinch of salt
  • ½ cup dairy-free chocolate chips
  • Brownie Layer
  • 3 eggs
  • ¾ cup (100g) maple sugar
  • ½ cup (80g) coconut sugar
  • 75g palm shortening (about ⅓ cup plus 1 tablespoon)
  • 150g chocolate, chopped
  • 2 tablespoons (15g) Dutch process chocolate
  • ½ cup (50g) blanched almond flour
  • ¼ cup (30g) arrowroot powder
  • 2 tablespoons (15g) coconut flour
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • ¼ teaspoon salt
  • ¾ teaspoon baking powder
Instructions
  1. Cookie Dough
  2. In the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with the paddle attachment, combine the melted palm shortening, maple syrup, and coconut sugar. Mix on medium speed until well combined and smooth.
  3. Add the egg and vanilla extract to the mixture in the stand mixer bowl. Mix on medium speed until thoroughly incorporated.
  4. Add almond flour, coconut flour, arrowroot, baking powder, baking soda, and a pinch of salt. Mix on high speed for 1 minute (no less!), stopping to scrape down the sides if necessary. Fold in chocolate chips using a spatula. Set the dough aside to rest and allow the coconut flour to absorb some of the moisture. Wipe down the bowl quickly to use for the brownie batter.
  5. Brownie Batter
  6. Preheat the oven to 325 degrees. Line a 9x9 inch baking dish with parchment paper or lightly grease it.
  7. Start by melting the palm shortening on the stove. Once melted, remove from heat and stir in the chocolate pieces until smooth. Let the mixture cool.
  8. In the stand mixer with a whisk attachment, beat the eggs for 5 minutes on high speed until they become fluffy and pale. DO NOT BEAT LESS THAN 5 MINUTES.
  9. While the eggs are being beaten, measure the maple sugar and coconut sugar, then add to the beaten eggs. Continue beating until well combined, 30 seconds to a minute.
  10. Gradually add the cooled chocolate and palm shortening mixture to the beaten eggs and sugar, mixing until thoroughly incorporated. Stir in the vanilla extract.
  11. Add almond flour, arrowroot powder, coconut flour, Dutch process chocolate, salt, and baking powder to the mixture. Gently fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture with a rubber spatula until just combined. Be careful not to overmix.
  12. If desired, fold in additional chocolate chips into the batter.
  13. Spread the brownie batter evenly into the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
  14. Drop spoonfuls of the cookie dough all around the top of the brownie batter and push a few into the brownie batter, leaving some on top with ribbons of brownie batter undisturbed.
  15. Bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 50 minutes, covering with foil after 30 minutes if the cookie layer is beginning to brown too much.
  16. Once baked, remove from the oven and let cool completely in the baking dish before slicing into squares and serving.
